headline: Dutch police arrest two suspects in bank fraud that allegedly used AI-generated calls
body: Rotterdam police arrested two suspects in a bank-helpdesk fraud that allegedly caused around €380,000 in losses for 170 victims in just three weeks. The suspects allegedly used AI-generated phone calls and a fake banking app to copy victims' bank cards remotely, allowing accomplices to withdraw thousands of euros. A Rotterdam court ruled on Tuesday that both men must remain in custody for at least another 90 days.
note: Victims were instructed to download an app, and police described this technical method as one they had not encountered before.

evidence.text: Rotterdam police arrested two suspects accused of a new form of bank-helpdesk fraud.
The operation allegedly caused around €380,000 in losses for 170 victims in just three weeks.
The suspects allegedly used AI-generated phone calls and a fake banking app to copy victims' bank cards remotely, allowing accomplices to withdraw thousands of euros.
A Rotterdam court's pretrial detention chamber ruled on Tuesday that both men must remain in custody for at least another 90 days while the investigation continues.
Victims were instructed to download an app and hold their bank cards against their phones to scan them.
Police described this technical method as one they had not encountered before.

The investigation began in mid-September, when Dutch banks reported cases of the new fraud method through the Electronic Crimes Task Force (ECTF), a partnership involving banks, police and prosecutors that shares information and expertise to tackle financial and digital crime.
